newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger's Black still eyeing control of Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger's Black still eyeing control of Fairfax.

text.p: Canadian press baron Conrad Black is still keen on controlling John Fairfax Holdings Ltd., although he is not optimistic that a quick decision on Australia's foreign ownership rules is in the offing.
"The prospect of being left in control of the company is one that I find rather pleasant," Black told Reuters in a telephone interview on Friday.

Black's Hollinger International Inc. owns 25 percent of Australian-based Fairfax. He has long expressed a desire to boost his holding and take control of the group, which owns the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper.

Black was responding to comments by News Corp. Ltd. Chairman Rupert Murdoch, who was quoted in one of his own newspapers, Brisbane's Courier-Mail, on Friday saying he had no interest in taking over the Fairfax newspaper group.
"(Murdoch's statement) is fairly humorous. It's a bit rich given the fact that he never stops telling me how much he would like to own Fairfax," Black said.
"I cannot obviously comment on what the others are doing or what Rupert's motives are. The fact is that he regularly expresses to me considerable hypothetical interest in Fairfax," he said.

Murdoch was quoted as saying that he did not wish to buy Fairfax and that he believed Kerry Packer, head of Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd., had no desire to own the group either. He said Packer tried three times in the past 12 months to sell his 15 percent stake in Fairfax.
Murdoch, who once described the classified sections of the Fairfax masthead newspapers as "rivers of gold", owns 5 percent of the group.
Packer is prevented by Australia's cross-media ownership rules from boosting his 15 percent holding while he owns the top rated Australian Nine Network.

"I think Mr. Black's going to be left with 25 percent of Fairfax and he's got to face up to running it because I don't think there's any buyer there, certainly at a premium," Murdoch was quoted as saying.

Black said he expected the Australian government to issue a report on cross-media ownership before the end of the year. But he was not convinced that a decision on foreign ownership rules would be forthcoming in the near future.
Black said interested parties were invited a couple of days ago to make submissions by the end of the month.
"This particular request for submissions ... I would not assume that it necessarily promises to resolve even the cross-media question, let alone the foreign ownership question," Black said.
Hollinger International plans to make a submission, Black said.
